messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Hi everyone,

is it possible to include SE when calling fscores with the full.scores option?

Best, Felix

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Not really, but you could just use some of the code already rolled
from the package like so:

###
library(mirt)
mod <- mirt(Science, 1)
scores <- fscores(mod)
scoremat <- scores[,c('F1', 'SE_F1')]

#verbatim from the package code
tabdata2 <- object@tabdatalong
tabdata2 <- tabdata2[,-ncol(tabdata2)]
stabdata2 <- apply(tabdata2, 1, paste, sep='', collapse = '/')
sfulldata <- apply(object@fulldata, 1, paste, sep='', collapse = '/')
scoremat <- scores[match(sfulldata, stabdata2), , drop = FALSE]
colnames(scoremat) <- colnames(scores)

head(scoremat)
###


Might be better to make a function do this, but I think you get the
idea. That's kind of a weird feature to include by default though, but
I guess if anyone else wants it then I'll consider adding it. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Dear Phil,

this is more generally, but could you give me some insight into EAP estimation of fscores? I wonder whether the prior distribution assumed is N(0,1) or it is somehow computed from the data?

Thanks, Felix

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Hi Felix,

The prior is usually as you suspect for unidimensional MAP and EAP
scores, N(0,1), or more generally, N ∼ (0, I) in the multivariate
exploratory case. This information comes from how you estimated the
latent covariance parameters, so for confirmatory/multiple group
models I will use the group parameters as indicators of the prior
distribution, while for single group the majority of the time it's the
standardized orthogonal multivariate normal. Use coef(), summary(), or
mod2values() on your object to locate the group parameters.

You can specify your own prior mean and covariances however if you
want something other than the model's 'group' parameters (possibly
something more diffuse). Naturally, making the prior more defuse will
influence the estimates less, and providing a sufficiently
uninformative prior to MAP estimation will give scores identical to ML
estimation (expect that extreme response patterns will still be
estimated and won't actually converge....). I've found this useful
when ML scores don't converge but you still want ML-like estimates, so
providing a poor prior will help to stabilize these response patterns
to obtain reasonable values while still not being overly influential.
Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 5095a73624617649
messages.subject: Re: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm wondering why when I call:
x2 <- mirt(frscores2, 1, itemtype='gpcm', SE=TRUE)
Instead of getting SE it seems like I get Confidence Intervals. Now, I know I can calculate SEs out of those, but given my estimations it would be very time consuming. Is there any other way I could directly get SEs together with the estimated parameters?

Thank you very much!
Best,
Olivia

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard error in fscores(..., full.scores=TRUE)
parts:
Hi Olivia,

I recently made the switch from reporting SE's to CI's for various
reasons. The reason primarily has to do with how the g and u SE's are
determined since they aren't symmetric about their values due to being
bounded between 0 and 1. Though I suppose it makes sense to include an
option to return the parameters with their standard errors instead.
I'll add this to the dev version the next chance I get, and it will
show up on the next major release.

In the meantime, if you are in a pinch you could find the SE's
manually through manipulating the information matrix to find the
parameter cov matrix. Use sqrt(diag(solve(model@information))) to
obtain the SE's for all estimated parameters. Cheers.

Phil
